headline: High: shared broad network/browser/MCP and API-key handling create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks; compliance risk is moderate.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents can run browsers and use broad network egress, so content from one can plausibly reach the other through web pages, files, or MCP-mediated workflows. next-ai-draw-io explicitly uses MCP and natural-language commands; RD-Agent uses browser/API-driven automation. No direct shared channel is documented, so I choose medium rather than low because the pathway exists in default-style workflows.
conditions: IF either agent ingests the other's generated text or files without provenance checks, prompt injection is possible.
IF an MCP bridge or shared workspace is introduced between them, attacker-controlled content can steer downstream actions.
mitigations: Disable automatic parsing of untrusted HTML/PDF/text as instructions.
Add provenance labels before passing outputs between agents.
Restrict MCP tools to allowlisted commands only.
Separate browser sessions and workspaces.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation guards.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both profiles show broad network egress and API-key handling, and both touch potentially sensitive work products. next-ai-draw-io handles API keys and documents; RD-Agent handles multiple API keys plus logs and execution traces. A shared workspace is not documented, so leakage is inferred rather than proven, but the default cloud/API surfaces make accidental disclosure plausible.
conditions: IF either agent writes secrets or sensitive documents into a shared directory, the other can read them.
IF either agent forwards file contents to external APIs, those contents may leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Store secrets in separate vault-backed env vars.
Keep per-agent workspaces on distinct directories.
Redact logs before sharing between agents.
Turn off automatic upload of full file contents where possible.
requires-engineering: enforce OS-level isolation between the two runtimes.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances and broad network/API use, but the profiles do not show overlapping write access to the same filesystem, git repo, or database. next-ai-draw-io is document-processing and RD-Agent is research automation, so conflict is possible only if an operator co-locates mutable resources. That makes this a low-severity overlap rather than medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory, they can overwrite each other's artifacts.
IF both are given the same mutable external resource, race conditions can corrupt state.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Serialize writes with a simple lock file.
Use read-only mounts for shared inputs.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same git branch.
requires-engineering: add resource-level locking in the orchestrator.

D_cascading_error.rationale: next-ai-draw-io produces AI-assisted visualizations from documents, and RD-Agent is an automation-oriented research agent. If RD-Agent consumes next-ai-draw-io outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect analyses or actions. The profiles do not prove direct action-taking, so medium is appropriate; uncertainty is resolved upward because the handoff pathway is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF RD-Agent treats diagrams or extracted text from next-ai-draw-io as ground truth, errors propagate downstream.
IF either agent acts on the other's output without verification, false assumptions can compound.
mitigations: Require human review before downstream actions.
Attach source links and confidence scores to outputs.
Compare outputs against original documents before use.
Limit RD-Agent to advisory mode for imported artifacts.
requires-engineering: add verification checkpoints between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents handle API keys and logs, but only RD-Agent explicitly touches logs/execution traces and multiple external APIs. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so this is not high; however, retention and logging differences can still create compliance gaps when sensitive documents or research data are processed across both systems.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are copied into RD-Agent logs or traces, retention policy mismatches can occur.
IF either agent processes regulated data through external APIs, residency or DPA obligations may be triggered.
mitigations: Minimize logged content in RD-Agent.
Keep regulated data out of external API calls.
Document retention periods for both systems.
Separate datasets by regulatory class.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
